title: Sales-CS request stitching and first-pass implementation estimator
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Sales and CS receive fragmented enterprise feature asks across multiple channels (email, Zendesk, Slack, demos). There is no lightweight process to stitch related asks for a single account or cohort, produce a concise one-page technical/economic estimate, and return a prioritized response to the account owner within 3 business days.

Goal: Create a lightweight 'stitch + estimator' workflow and template that enables CS/Sales to bundle related enterprise requests, apply a rapid implementation complexity score and cost proxy, and get a PM-approved first-pass scoping note back within 72 hours. This should reduce back-and-forth, speed decisioning, and surface high-impact asks to PM/Eng prioritization queues.

Scope:
- In-scope: Build the request stitching pattern, a short rubric for implementation complexity (integration surface, data sensitivity, runtime changes, UI work), an economics proxy (P0/P1 cost band), and a CS-facing template and playbook. Integrate with our intake tracker dashboard (Sales Intake Board) and generate a compact PRD-lite link for PM review.
- Out-of-scope: Full technical specs, engineering tickets created automatically, guaranteed timeline commitments, or changes to billing/contracting workflows.

Acceptance criteria:
1) CS can submit a bundled intake using the new template within Sales Intake Board and receive a PM response tag within 72 hours.
2) The estimator produces complexity (Low/Medium/High) and a cost band (Quick, Moderate, Significant) based on the rubric.
3) PMs can triage and mark items for 'evaluate', 'requires eng', or 'not feasible' with short rationale.
4) Links to a Confluence PRD-lite and a recommended next-step (pilot, backlog, discovery) are generated and surfaced to the account owner.

Trade-offs and considerations:
- Keep rubric conservative to avoid overpromising; prefer false negatives (underestimate feasibility) over false positives.
- Manual review by a PM is required for all High complexity buckets to control scope creep.
- We prioritize speed for 72-hour response; accuracy will improve iteratively with calibration against historical closed requests.
